### REMED-GFX-064 — SdlGpu + D3D12: `GraphicsDevice.Viewport` wired to the GPU — DONE and VERIFIED

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Sev / Pri / Owner / Status | MEDIUM / P2 / GRAPHICS / **DONE and VERIFIED (both backends; SdlGpu runtime, D3D12 off-screen runtime under Wine+vkd3d-proton)** |
| Commits | SdlGpu test `dce6e9d2`, SdlGpu fix `4689cfcb`, D3D12 test `52908242`, D3D12 fix `963fbf23`, docs (this entry) |
| Root cause (both) | Neither backend overrode the **no-op** base `IGraphicsBackend::SetViewport(...)` (`IGraphicsBackend.hpp:687`, empty `{}`). **SdlGpu** never called `SDL_SetGPUViewport` anywhere; **D3D12** hardcoded `D3D12_VIEWPORT{0,0,boundColorWidth_,boundColorHeight_,0,1}` at all four `RSSetViewports` sites plus the SpriteBatch flush. A custom `GraphicsDevice.Viewport` was a total no-op on **both** — backbuffer **and** RT — broader than GFX-062 (Vulkan RT-only). Hypothesis CONFIRMED for both; **not** the same root cause internally (see below), so treated as two independent slices under one ID. |

**The two backends needed DIFFERENT solutions (verified, not assumed — task Phase 5 caution honored).**

**SdlGpu — deferred, same shape as Vulkan GFX-062 → per-draw capture.** SdlGpu queues every draw (`drawOrder_`) and replays it at `Present()` inside a per-target render pass; `GraphicsDevice::SetRenderTarget` resets the frame-global `Viewport` to the target's full size on bind **and** unbind (`ResetViewportAndScissorForRenderTarget`). So a per-pass read of the live viewport (which is exactly how the existing SdlGpu scissor works) would apply the post-unbind full-**backbuffer** viewport to the RT pass. Fixed by capturing the viewport **per draw** at enqueue:
1. `SetViewport()` stores `viewportSet_/X_/Y_/W_/H_/minDepth/maxDepth` (store-only, never read back at set time).
2. `QueuedDrawRef` carries a viewport snapshot; new `PushDrawOrder()` (replacing all **9** raw `drawOrder_.push_back({Kind,idx})` sites — the 8 3D families + sprite) tags each queued draw with the live viewport.
3. `RenderQueuedDraws()` applies `SDL_SetGPUViewport` **per draw** via new `ApplyViewportForRef()`: the ref's captured sub-region if set (unclamped rect — a transform not a clip; top-left `y`, no extra flip since the sprite/3D shaders already handle SDL clip-space Y; depth clamped `[0,1]`), else the pass's full render-target extents (byte-identical to pre-fix = SDL's own default full-target viewport).

**D3D12 — immediate-per-draw → store + consume (NOT D3D11-copy, NOT capture/replay).** Every D3D12 draw re-records its own command list (`Reset`→record→`Close`→`ExecuteCommandListAndWaitEXT`), so there is no persistent context to `RSSetViewports` into at `SetViewport` time (D3D11's model) and no deferral needing capture/replay (Vulkan/SdlGpu's model). Fixed by:
1. `SetViewport()` stores the rect + depth range.
2. New `GetEffectiveViewportEXT()` returns the stored custom viewport if set (unclamped rect, top-left `TopLeftY`, depth clamped `[0,1]`), else the full bound-target rect (byte-identical to the old hardcode). Read at all four backend `RSSetViewports` sites (`DrawColoredPrimitives`, `DrawIndexedColoredPrimitives`, `DrawPrimitivesExImpl`, `DrawInstancedPrimitivesEx`) and the `D3D12SpriteBatch` flush (via `owner_`).
3. Target-change resets the stored viewport (`viewportSet_=false`) in `BindOffscreenColorTargetEXT`/`UnbindOffscreenColorTargetEXT` (covering MRT-bind + backbuffer-restore, which delegate through them) — mirrors XNA's `SetRenderTarget` reset (also driven by GraphicsDevice) and prevents a stale viewport leaking across targets in backend-direct callers.

**MinDepth/MaxDepth (Phase 16).** Inseparable from the fix on both backends: the stored viewport carries `minDepth/maxDepth`, clamped to `[0,1]` (SDL_GPUViewport / D3D12_VIEWPORT valid domain, = XNA's own valid range), and feeds the same viewport struct — so honoring the viewport necessarily honors its depth range. Both APIs expose a real configurable depth range (unlike some backends), so no deviation to record. Not separately depth-probed (a depth-range pixel test needs a depth buffer + Z-specific draw; same scope call as GFX-062), but wired and carried through — verified by code, matching the GFX-062 precedent.

**SpriteBatch (Phases 6/7).** The GPU viewport **rectangle** is now honored for sprite draws on both backends (SdlGpu sprite draws go through the same per-draw `ApplyViewportForRef`; D3D12 sprite flush reads `GetEffectiveViewportEXT`). The sprite **projection** `ViewportSize` uniform (used for the pixel→NDC ortho transform) is deliberately left at the full-target/virtual-resolution size on both — changing it to the viewport's W/H (which FNA `SpriteEffect.OnApply` and D3D11's `RSGetViewports`-readback both do) is a separate cross-backend sprite-projection parity nuance, byte-identical when no custom viewport is set, and out of scope for the GPU-viewport-rectangle wiring this task is about. Recorded here honestly; not a regression (existing sprite tests never set a custom viewport).

**Tests.**
- **SdlGpu** — new `examples/sdlgpu_rendertarget_viewport_test.cpp` (`SdlGpu_RenderTargetViewport`, `cmake/Tests/SdlGpuTests.cmake`). Asymmetric 80×60 `RenderTarget2D`, read back via `RenderTarget2D::GetData` (SdlGpu can't download the swapchain — SDLGPU-39). 3 frames / **14** checks: custom sub-region viewport (13,9,31,23) 5-way probe; full-viewport control; **two viewports in one frame** (the per-draw-capture crux — RED into A, GREEN into B, unbind, read; a per-pass read would leave the whole target GREEN).
- **D3D12** — new Check VP in `examples/d3d12_smoke_test.cpp` (the off-screen, plain-Wine-safe CTest). Asymmetric 80×60 off-screen RT via `BindOffscreenColorTargetEXT`, read back via the `ReadBackRenderTargetFull` READBACK-buffer technique. **11** checks: custom sub-region (5-way probe), full-viewport control, two viewports/two draws into one target.

**Pre-fix vs post-fix (runtime).** SdlGpu `SdlGpu_RenderTargetViewport` **7/14 → 14/14** (llvmpipe/Vulkan, Xvfb :99): pre-fix the custom viewport was fully ignored (all outside probes RED) and the two-viewport frame was entirely GREEN (last full-size draw wins). D3D12 Check VP **4/11 → 11/11** (Wine+vkd3d-proton, off-screen): identical failure signature pre-fix.

**Backbuffer (Phase 4).** SdlGpu backbuffer readback is blocked (SDLGPU-39) so the SdlGpu viewport is proven on an RT pass (which exercises the identical per-draw `ApplyViewportForRef` code path as the backbuffer pass). D3D12 has no windowed backbuffer under Wine (REMED-BUILD-012), so its viewport is proven on the off-screen target (identical `GetEffectiveViewportEXT` path as every draw). Both fixes are pass/target-agnostic by construction — the same code services backbuffer and RT.

**Regression.** SdlGpu full shard **28/28** (incl. RT/RTCube/MRT/sprite/orientation/scissor/effects — zero regressions). D3D12 `d3d12_smoke_test` **220/231**: the 11 FAILs (N3c/N5/O4/P4/Q4/S1/S2/S4/S5/U4/V2 — all DX-137 fog / DX-135 skinned) are **pre-existing and identical with the changes stashed** (measured both ways) — **zero regressions**; my change has no causal path to fog blending or bone skinning.

**Validation (Phase 10).** SdlGpu runs on SDL_gpu's Vulkan driver with debug mode enabled (`SDL_CreateGPUDevice` debug_mode); the new `SDL_SetGPUViewport` calls use non-negative, in-bounds-or-full-target rects (degenerate → full-target fallback) and produced no new validation output across the 28-test shard. REMED-GFX-059 (VUID-…-02684) is a separate, pre-existing SdlGpu item, not touched.

**Generated shaders.** None — zero `.glsl/.vert/.frag/.spv/.hlsl/.wgsl/.dxbc/bytecode` diff across all four commits (pure command/state handling; Viewport is rasterizer/command state).

**Sanitizers.** New arithmetic is float casts + `std::clamp(minDepth/maxDepth, 0, 1)` and a `w>0 && h>0` guard; degenerate/unset viewports fall back to the full target, so no negative/zero-extent viewport reaches SDL or D3D12. No new bounds arithmetic warranting a dedicated UBSan build (same reasoning as GFX-062).

**Cross-backend parity (Phase 19).** After GFX-062 (Vulkan) + GFX-063 (Bgfx) + this (SdlGpu, D3D12), all backends now honor a custom `GraphicsDevice.Viewport` in RT passes; EasyGL/D3D11/D3D9 already did (immediate), WebGPU per-pass. SdlGpu compared runtime directly (14/14); D3D12 compared at runtime off-screen (11/11) — the real-window path stays BUILD-012-blocked but the off-screen path executes the identical viewport code.

**New findings.** **GFX-068** (SdlGpu per-pass scissor reset-to-full-backbuffer on RT unbind) — surfaced when the viewport∩scissor frame could not isolate the intersection on SdlGpu (GetData requires unbind; unbind resets the per-pass scissor). Independent of the viewport wiring (scissor, per-pass vs per-draw), recorded below, not fixed. The viewport∩scissor **independence** itself is already proven on Vulkan (GFX-062 Frame 3), where both states are per-draw.

| Affected files | `include/CNA/Internal/Backends/SdlGpu/SdlGpuGraphicsBackend.hpp`, `src/CNA/Internal/Backends/SdlGpu/SdlGpuGraphicsBackend.cpp`, `examples/sdlgpu_rendertarget_viewport_test.cpp`, `cmake/Tests/SdlGpuTests.cmake`, `include/CNA/Internal/Backends/D3D12/D3D12GraphicsBackend.hpp`, `src/CNA/Internal/Backends/D3D12/D3D12GraphicsBackend.cpp`, `src/CNA/Internal/Backends/D3D12/D3D12SpriteBatch.cpp`, `examples/d3d12_smoke_test.cpp` |
| Backends / Platforms | SdlGpu, D3D12 / ALL |

### REMED-GFX-068 — SdlGpu: `ScissorRectangle` now captured & replayed PER DRAW (per-pass reset-to-backbuffer on RT unbind) — DONE and VERIFIED

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Sev / Pri / Owner / Status | LOW / P3 / GRAPHICS / **DONE and VERIFIED (SdlGpu runtime, Xvfb :99, llvmpipe/Vulkan debug mode)** |
| Commits | test `38ffda25`, fix `9e65ac4e`, docs (this entry) |
| Root cause | SdlGpu applied `ScissorRectangle` **once per pass** from the live member state at `Present()` time (`ApplyScissorForPass(pass, targetW, targetH)`, gated on `scissorEnabled_`), unlike the **per-draw** viewport GFX-064 wired. In this deferred backend every draw is queued (`drawOrder_`) and replayed at Present in a per-target pass; a game that sets a scissor while a RenderTarget2D is bound and then unbinds it triggers `GraphicsDevice::ResetViewportAndScissorForRenderTarget` → `setScissorRectangleProperty(0,0,backbufferW,backbufferH)` — so by the time the RT pass replays, the live scissor rect is the full **backbuffer** (larger than the RT) and the scissor no longer clips. Exact deferred-model shape of Vulkan GFX-013 (scissor) and SdlGpu GFX-064 (viewport). |

**The fix (mirrors GFX-064's per-draw viewport capture).**
1. `QueuedDrawRef` carries a scissor snapshot (`scissorEnabled` + `scissorX/Y/W/H`), alongside the GFX-064 viewport snapshot.
2. `PushDrawOrder()` (the single centralized append point GFX-064 established across the 9 `drawOrder_.push_back` sites — 8 3D families + sprite) captures the live `scissorEnabled_` (from `ApplyRasterizerState`'s `ScissorTestEnable`) and `scissorX_/Y_/W_/H_` (from `SetScissorRect`) into each queued draw.
3. `RenderQueuedDraws()` applies `SDL_SetGPUScissor` **per draw** via new `ApplyScissorForRef()`, immediately after the existing `ApplyViewportForRef()` — so each draw honors the scissor it was enqueued under. The 3 per-pass `ApplyScissorForPass()` calls (swapchain / RenderToTarget / RenderToTargetCubeFace) are removed; SDL sets a default full-target scissor at pass begin which each draw then overrides.
4. `ApplyScissorForRef()` clamps the captured rect to the target's **physical extent** in int64 (a scissor is a **clip**, unlike the viewport's NDC→framebuffer transform which is passed unclamped) — offset ≥ 0, offset+extent within the target, no overflow — mirroring `VulkanGraphicsBackend::computeScissor` (GFX-013). `scissorEnabled=false` or a zero-size rect ⇒ full target (no clip), matching `RasterizerState.ScissorTestEnable=false`.

**SDL GPU scissor API semantics (Phase 7/8).** `SDL_SetGPUScissor(render_pass, SDL_Rect*)` sets per-command-buffer scissor state that persists until changed — exactly like `SDL_SetGPUViewport` (so scissor *does* have a per-draw equivalent; the old header comment claiming it did not was wrong and is corrected). `SDL_BeginGPURenderPass` "automatically sets a default viewport and scissor" = the full target, so an unset/disabled scissor needs no explicit call. There is no separate "disable scissor" call — a disabled scissor is represented by the full-target rect.

**Coordinate / Y semantics (Phase 9).** `SDL_Rect` is top-left origin, matching XNA `ScissorRectangle` directly — **no Y-flip** (same as Vulkan `VkRect2D`, GFX-013; SDL_gpu normalizes framebuffer orientation across its Vulkan/Metal/D3D12 drivers). The test's asymmetric above/below probes (y=3 vs y=30 around a y[8,21) scissor) prove orientation.

**Physical target extent (Phase 10).** `ApplyScissorForRef` clamps to the pass's own render-target extents (`target.rt->width/height`, `cube->size`, or `physicalWidth_/Height_` for the swapchain) — never the backbuffer size while an RT is bound, never the viewport size. The test's 64×48 RT ≠ 96×72 backbuffer catches any dimension leak.

**Viewport interaction (Phase 11).** Both dynamic states are now per-draw and independent. Frame 3 uses non-coincident Viewport `(8,6,40,30)` and Scissor `(20,4,30,20)`: the visible region is exactly the intersection — a scissor-clipped-but-in-viewport probe and a viewport-clipped-but-in-scissor probe are both BLACK, the intersection interior RED.

**SpriteBatch vs 3D (Phase 12).** Covered by construction: `ApplyScissorForRef` runs for **every** `QueuedDrawRef` before the draw-kind switch, so all 8 3D families **and** the `Sprite` kind (which enqueues via the same `PushDrawOrder(DrawKind::Sprite,…)`) get the identical per-draw scissor — the same single code path GFX-064's viewport uses. The new test exercises the 3D path; the passing `SdlGpu_2D`/`SdlGpu_RenderState` shard exercises sprites through the same replay loop.

**Render-target types (Phase 13).** RenderTarget2D, RenderTargetCube, and MRT share the one `RenderQueuedDraws` replay path (each begins a pass then calls it), so the single `ApplyScissorForRef` change services all three. The regression targets RenderTarget2D directly; Cube/MRT are covered by construction + the passing `SdlGpu_RenderTargetCube`/`SdlGpu_MRT` shard.

**Backbuffer (Phase 14).** The swapchain pass uses the identical per-draw `ApplyScissorForRef` path (SdlGpu can't read the swapchain back — SDLGPU-39 — so it's proven on the RT pass, byte-identical code). Frame 1's scissor-OFF control guards against the fix over-applying a stored rect when `ScissorTestEnable=false`.

| Test | `examples/sdlgpu_rendertarget_scissor_test.cpp` (`SdlGpu_RenderTargetScissor`, `cmake/Tests/SdlGpuTests.cmake`). Asymmetric 64×48 `RenderTarget2D` (≠ 96×72 backbuffer), read back via `RenderTarget2D::GetData` **after unbind** (the realistic case the pre-existing `SdlGpu_RenderState` Check F structurally avoided by reading *before* unbind). 4 frames / **17** checks: F0 scissor ON 5-way probe; F1 scissor OFF control; F2 three scissor states in one pass (disabled-BLUE background + scissor-A-RED + scissor-B-GREEN — the per-draw-capture crux); F3 Viewport∩Scissor intersection. |
| Pre-fix vs post-fix (runtime) | **9/17 → 17/17.** Pre-fix: F0 left/right/above/below RED not BLACK (scissor inert on the RT after unbind); F2 entirely GREEN (all three draws share the post-unbind full-backbuffer scissor, last full draw wins); F3 scissor-clip probe RED not BLACK. Post-fix all 17 pass, stable across repeated runs. |
| Validation (Phase 18) | SdlGpu runs on SDL_gpu's Vulkan driver with `debug_mode`. Post-fix: **zero** validation errors across repeated runs of the new test (the clamped rects always satisfy the scissor VUIDs). REMED-GFX-059 (`VUID-vkCmdDraw-renderPass-02684`, depth-stencil attachment) is a separate pre-existing item — it appeared in the *pre-fix* run of this test but not post-fix; left classified separately, not touched. |
| Regression (Phase 19) | Full SdlGpu shard **29/29** (28 pre-existing + the new test): incl. `SdlGpu_RenderState` (scissor Check F, same path), `SdlGpu_RenderTargetViewport` (GFX-064), `SdlGpu_RenderTarget2D/Cube/MRT`, and the GFX-006 (`SdlGpu_SkinnedEffect_WorldNormal`) / GFX-007 (`SdlGpu_EnvMapEmissive`) / GFX-009 (`SdlGpu_*_Fog`) / GFX-010 (`SdlGpu_ViewSpace_Fog`) controls — zero regressions. |

### REMED-GFX-069 — SdlGpu: `GraphicsDevice.BlendFactor` (constant blend color) captured & replayed PER DRAW — DONE and VERIFIED

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Sev / Pri / Owner / Status | LOW / P3 / GRAPHICS / **DONE and VERIFIED (SdlGpu runtime, Xvfb :99, llvmpipe/Vulkan debug mode)** |
| Commits | test `38f43747`, fix `cf689000`, docs (this entry) |
| Root cause | SdlGpu's `ToBlendFactor`/`FillBlendState` correctly map XNA `Blend::BlendFactor`(10)→`SDL_GPU_BLENDFACTOR_CONSTANT_COLOR` and `Blend::InverseBlendFactor`(11)→`SDL_GPU_BLENDFACTOR_ONE_MINUS_CONSTANT_COLOR` into the baked pipeline, but the backend **never overrode the no-op base `IGraphicsBackend::SetBlendFactor(float,float,float,float)`** (`IGraphicsBackend.hpp:674`, empty `{}`) and **never called `SDL_SetGPUBlendConstants` anywhere**. So the constant those two blend factors multiply by was SDL_gpu's own driver-default blend constant, never `GraphicsDevice.BlendFactor`. Exact blend-constant analog of GFX-064 ("never overrode base `SetViewport`"). |

**XNA/FNA BlendFactor semantics (Phase 2).** `GraphicsDevice.BlendFactor` is a `Color` (default `Color::White` = `(1,1,1,1)`) applied atomically both by its own setter and as part of assigning a `BlendState` (`GraphicsDevice::setBlendStateProperty` → `setBlendFactorProperty(state.BlendFactor)`; a `BlendState`'s own default `BlendFactor` is also `White`). `setBlendFactorProperty` pushes it to the backend as **already-normalized `[0,1]` linear floats** (`R/255,G/255,B/255,A/255` — `GraphicsDevice.cpp:1745`). It must take effect immediately for subsequent draws, persist until changed, and NOT require constructing a new `BlendState`. `SetRenderTarget` does **not** reset `BlendFactor` (unlike Viewport/Scissor, which `ResetViewportAndScissorForRenderTarget` does) — but per-draw capture is still required because SdlGpu is deferred (see below).

**SDL GPU blend-constant API / state lifetime (Phase 8).** `SDL_SetGPUBlendConstants(SDL_GPURenderPass*, SDL_FColor)` (SDL 3.2.0) — "Sets the current blend constants on a command buffer." `SDL_FColor` is `{float r,g,b,a}`. It is render-pass/command-buffer dynamic state that persists until changed, exactly like `SDL_SetGPUScissor`/`SDL_SetGPUViewport`/`SDL_SetGPUStencilReference`. `SDL_BeginGPURenderPass` sets a default viewport+scissor but says nothing about blend constants, so an unset constant is SDL_gpu's driver default (see pre-fix evidence). Not assumed to equal Vulkan semantics — read from the repo's pinned `SDL_gpu.h`.

**Why per-draw capture (the deferred model).** SdlGpu queues every draw (`drawOrder_`) and replays them at `Present()` inside per-target passes. A single stored `blendFactor_` read at replay would give **every** queued draw the LAST `BlendFactor` set that frame (and, across a bind→unbind→backbuffer sequence, the post-unbind value). So the constant is snapshotted **per draw at enqueue** — the identical mechanism GFX-064 (viewport) and GFX-068 (scissor) established.

**The fix (mirrors GFX-064/068).**
1. `SetBlendFactor()` override — **store-only** into `blendFactorR_/G_/B_/A_` (default `1,1,1,1` = XNA `Color::White`, so draws that predate any `SetBlendFactor` use the correct XNA default rather than SDL_gpu's arbitrary uninitialized constant).
2. `QueuedDrawRef` carries `blendFactorR/G/B/A`; `PushDrawOrder()` (the single centralized append point across the 9 draw families + sprite) captures the live members into each queued draw, alongside the viewport/scissor snapshots.
3. `RenderQueuedDraws()` applies `SDL_SetGPUBlendConstants` **per draw** via new `ApplyBlendFactorForRef()`, immediately after `ApplyScissorForRef()`. Applied **unconditionally** — the constant is inert for any pipeline whose blend factors don't reference `CONSTANT_COLOR`/`ONE_MINUS_CONSTANT_COLOR`, so no gating on the current `BlendState` is needed (Phase 12: correctness-first; same "always set, harmlessly overwritten for non-target refs" property as viewport/scissor).

**Channel / alpha mapping (Phases 3/5/13).** `SDL_FColor{ref.blendFactorR, G, B, A}` — direct R→r, G→g, B→b, A→a. No BGRA swap, no premultiply, no sRGB transfer (a numeric pipeline factor, not a framebuffer color). The alpha channel feeds the **alpha** blend-factor slot: `FillBlendState` maps `Alpha{Source,Destination}Blend == BlendFactor` to `CONSTANT_COLOR` too, and `CONSTANT_COLOR` uses the constant's `.a` for the alpha component — so `SDL_SetGPUBlendConstants`' single RGBA call services both color and alpha factors (proven by Frame 3: `AlphaSrc=BlendFactor` yields `A ≈ 153` = `constant.a`).

**Pipeline-cache interaction (Phase 16).** The blend-factor **value** is NOT in `PipelineCacheKey` — only the blend-factor **enums** (`colorSrc/colorDst/alphaSrc/alphaDst/colorFunc/alphaFunc`, i.e. whether `CONSTANT_COLOR` is used) are hashed. The constant lives in `QueuedDrawRef`, not `RenderStateSnapshot`, so it never fragments the cache. Proven at runtime by Frame 4: three different constants (RED/GREEN/BLUE) drawn through **one** `BlendState` instance → one pipeline → three correct results (no pipeline-per-constant explosion).

| Test | `examples/sdlgpu_rendertarget_blendfactor_test.cpp` (`SdlGpu_RenderTargetBlendFactor`, `cmake/Tests/SdlGpuTests.cmake`). 64×48 `RenderTarget2D` (≠ 96×72 backbuffer), read back via `RenderTarget2D::GetData` **after unbind**. Distinctive constant `(64,128,192,153)` (distinct per channel — also catches BGRA swap → `192,128,64`, white → `255,255,255`, zero → `0,0,0`). 6 frames / **8** checks: F0 source-side `BlendFactor` (`white*constant`); F1 `InverseBlendFactor` (`white*(1-constant)`); F2 destination-side `BlendFactor` (`dest white * constant`); F3 alpha-channel constant (`AlphaSrc=BlendFactor` → `constant.a`); F4 **three `BlendFactor`s in one pass over three disjoint regions**, changing **only** `GraphicsDevice.BlendFactor` (RED/GREEN/BLUE — the per-draw-capture crux; also proves Phase 15 change-factor-not-state and Phase 16 dynamic-not-baked); F5 **SpriteBatch** path (white texture through a `BlendFactor` blend state — same `PushDrawOrder`/`QueuedDrawRef` path as 3D). |
| Pre-fix vs post-fix (runtime) | **0/8 → 8/8.** Pre-fix every constant-color blend used the driver default (observed `(1,1,1,1)` on llvmpipe → F0/F2/F5 white, F1 black, F3 `A=255`, F4 all white). Post-fix all 8 pass with exact values (`(64,128,192)`, `(191,127,63)`, `A=153`, RED/GREEN/BLUE), stable across repeated runs. |
| BlendState variants (Phase 14) | Covered: A source=`BlendFactor`/dst=`Zero` (F0); B source=`InverseBlendFactor`/dst=`Zero` (F1); C source=`One`/dst=`BlendFactor` (F2, destination side); E constant-alpha factor (F3). Both source- and destination-side consumption confirmed. |
| Backbuffer vs RT (Phases 6/18) | The swapchain pass uses the identical per-draw `ApplyBlendFactorForRef` path (SdlGpu can't read the swapchain back — SDLGPU-39 — so it's proven on the RT pass, byte-identical code, target-agnostic by construction). F4's multi-constant-in-one-pass exercises the state-timing that a per-pass read would fail; no BlendFactor leak across draws (each region shows only its own constant). |
| Validation (Phase 19) | SdlGpu runs on SDL_gpu's Vulkan driver with `debug_mode`. Post-fix: **zero** validation errors across repeated runs (blend constants have no VUIDs to violate with in-range floats). REMED-GFX-059 (`VUID-vkCmdDraw-renderPass-02684`, depth-stencil attachment) is a separate pre-existing item; it surfaced in the *pre-fix* run of this test but not post-fix (same intermittent behavior GFX-068 noted) — left classified separately, not touched. |
| Regression (Phase 21) | Full SdlGpu shard **30/30** (29 pre-existing + the new test): incl. `SdlGpu_RenderState` (blend/depth/stencil dynamic state), `SdlGpu_RenderTargetViewport` (GFX-064), `SdlGpu_RenderTargetScissor` (GFX-068), `SdlGpu_2D`/`3D`/RT2D/Cube/MRT/sprite, and the GFX-006 (`SdlGpu_SkinnedEffect_WorldNormal`) / GFX-007 (`SdlGpu_EnvMapEmissive`) / GFX-009 (`SdlGpu_*_Fog`) / GFX-010 (`SdlGpu_ViewSpace_Fog`) controls — zero regressions. |
| Cross-backend parity (Phase 20) | The dedicated reference tests `EasyGL_BlendState_BlendFactor` and `Bgfx_BlendState_BlendFactor` both PASS (rebuilt+run), confirming the XNA semantics SdlGpu now matches (a `BlendFactor` blend of a white source yields the constant color). Vulkan/EasyGL/Bgfx/D3D11/D3D9/WebGPU already override `SetBlendFactor`; SdlGpu was the sole backend using the no-op base. **New finding GFX-070** surfaced here (Vulkan sets blend constants once/frame despite declaring `VK_DYNAMIC_STATE_BLEND_CONSTANTS`). |
| Generated shaders | None — zero `.glsl/.vert/.frag/.spv/.hlsl/.wgsl/.dxbc/bytecode` diff (pure command/state handling; blend constant is dynamic pipeline state). |
| Sanitizers | New arithmetic is trivial: 4 float member copies + 4 float copies into the POD `QueuedDrawRef` snapshot (default-initialized to `1.0f`) + an `SDL_FColor` aggregate init. No bounds arithmetic, no negative/oversized values reach SDL (normalization is done upstream in `GraphicsDevice`). No dedicated UBSan build warranted (same reasoning as GFX-064/068). |
| Deferred-state sweep (Phase 22) | Enumerated every `SDL_SetGPU*` dynamic pass-state call in the backend: `SDL_SetGPUViewport` (per-draw, GFX-064), `SDL_SetGPUScissor` (per-draw, GFX-068), `SDL_SetGPUBlendConstants` (per-draw, this), `SDL_SetGPUStencilReference` (per-draw via `command.renderState.stencilReference`, captured at enqueue in `CaptureRenderState` — enqueue-time capture, immune to deferred-replay staleness). `SDL_SetGPUSwapchainParameters` is device/swapchain config, not per-draw. **No remaining SdlGpu stale-state defect** — all four SDL_gpu per-draw dynamic states are now correctly per-draw. |
| New findings | **GFX-070** — Vulkan blend-constant per-frame single-set (see note below). |
| Affected files | `include/CNA/Internal/Backends/SdlGpu/SdlGpuGraphicsBackend.hpp`, `src/CNA/Internal/Backends/SdlGpu/SdlGpuGraphicsBackend.cpp`, `examples/sdlgpu_rendertarget_blendfactor_test.cpp`, `cmake/Tests/SdlGpuTests.cmake` |
| Backends / Platforms | SdlGpu / ALL |

### REMED-GFX-070 — Vulkan: blend constants set once per frame despite `VK_DYNAMIC_STATE_BLEND_CONSTANTS` (DONE and VERIFIED, 2026-07-21)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Sev / Pri / Owner / Status | LOW / P3 / GRAPHICS / **DONE and VERIFIED (Vulkan runtime, Xvfb :99, llvmpipe/Lavapipe, validation layer loaded)** |
| Commits | test `dfc1b332`, fix `815b33df`, docs (this entry) |
| Evidence | Vulkan pipelines declare `VK_DYNAMIC_STATE_BLEND_CONSTANTS` (`VulkanGraphicsBackend.cpp:2438,2625,2958,3323,4900,5035`), so the constant MUST be set per command buffer via `vkCmdSetBlendConstants`. But there is **exactly one** `vkCmdSetBlendConstants` call in the whole backend — `RecordCommandBuffer` line 6926, at the **backbuffer** pass begin (Phase 2), reading the live `blendFactorR_/G_/B_/A_` members. |
| Consequence | (a) **RT passes (Phase 1) run before that single set** → RenderTarget2D/Cube/MRT constant-color blends execute with an undefined/stale blend constant (the dynamic state is never set that frame before them: the RT pass-begin at 6861-6870 sets `vkCmdSetViewport`+`vkCmdSetScissor` but NOT blend constants, and `draw3DFor`/`drawSpritesFor` apply per-draw viewport/scissor but NOT blend constants). (b) The backbuffer pass sets the constant **once from the live member**, so multiple `GraphicsDevice.BlendFactor` values within one backbuffer frame collapse to the last one set (last-wins), not per-draw. This is the Vulkan analog of GFX-069: viewport/scissor were converted to per-draw dynamic capture by GFX-062/013, but blend constants were left as a single per-frame set. |

**Phase 1 — source reconciliation (CONFIRMED at HEAD).**
- **Only `vkCmdSetBlendConstants` call:** `RecordCommandBuffer` line 6926, inside the Phase-2 backbuffer pass, immediately after the pass-begin `vkCmdSetViewport` (6917) / `vkCmdSetScissor` (6922), reading `float bc[4] = { blendFactorR_, blendFactorG_, blendFactorB_, blendFactorA_ }` — the live frame-global members.
- **RT vs backbuffer paths DIFFER:** the Phase-1 RT pass (6861-6873) sets viewport (6868) and scissor (6870) at pass-begin but **never** sets blend constants, and neither `draw3DFor` nor `drawSpritesFor` (which DO apply per-draw viewport/scissor via `computeViewport`/`computeScissor`) touch blend constants. So RT-pass draws have blend constants that were never set in the command buffer that frame (undefined per Vulkan spec; possibly a stale value retained from a prior frame's backbuffer set).
- **SpriteBatch vs 3D share the SAME BlendFactor source:** both read the backend's `blendFactorR_/G_/B_/A_` frame-global members (set by `SetBlendFactor`, 8157). Neither captures per draw/batch (unlike scissor/viewport, which `BatchSnapshot`/`Pending3DDraw` already snapshot).
- **BlendFactor is NOT captured anywhere** — the only reference outside `SetBlendFactor` is the single record-time read at 6925.
- **Pipeline mapping is CORRECT:** `ToVkBlendFactor` (3048) maps XNA `Blend::BlendFactor`(10)→`VK_BLEND_FACTOR_CONSTANT_COLOR` (3060) and `Blend::InverseBlendFactor`(11)→`VK_BLEND_FACTOR_ONE_MINUS_CONSTANT_COLOR` (3061); `FillBlendAttachmentState` applies them to both color and alpha slots (3108-3112). The blend-factor **value** is not a pipeline-cache key (`PackBlendBits` hashes only the blend-factor *enums*, 3087-3096) — so the constant is genuinely dynamic state, as the pipeline declares.
- **Constant-alpha semantics CORRECT by construction:** `vkCmdSetBlendConstants(cb, float[4])` takes `{R,G,B,A}`; for a `VK_BLEND_FACTOR_CONSTANT_COLOR` alpha blend factor, Vulkan uses the constant's `.a` component — so a single RGBA set services both the color and alpha factor slots (same as GFX-069's SdlGpu finding).

**Phase 2 — XNA/FNA semantics (independently reconfirmed for Vulkan).** `GraphicsDevice::setBlendFactorProperty` (`GraphicsDevice.cpp:1741`) pushes the Color to the backend as already-normalized `[0,1]` floats `SetBlendFactor(R/255,G/255,B/255,A/255)` (1745-1749) — backend-agnostic, identical to the path GFX-069 established for SdlGpu. It takes effect immediately for subsequent draws, persists until changed, and is applied atomically as part of assigning a `BlendState` (1686). Unlike Viewport/Scissor, `SetRenderTarget` does **not** reset `BlendFactor` — but per-draw capture is still required on Vulkan because the recorder is whole-frame-deferred (multiple BlendFactor values in one frame otherwise collapse to last-wins, and RT passes get no set at all).

**Phase 9 — backbuffer control (predicted).** A single-BlendFactor backbuffer scene works *accidentally* today: `Vulkan_BlendState_BlendFactor` (backbuffer, reads midtone `(200,100,0)` ±15) passes because the one frame-global set at 6926 == the only BlendFactor that frame. Multiple values in one backbuffer frame → last-wins; any RT use → no set at all. To be verified at runtime.

**Phase 10 — deferred-state model / where lifetime is lost.** `SetBlendFactor` writes frame-global `blendFactorR_/…` → draws enqueue into `pending3D_`/`activeBatches_` **without** snapshotting the constant → `RecordCommandBuffer` reads the frame-global member exactly once (6925) at backbuffer-pass begin. The lifetime is lost at enqueue: the constant a draw should use is overwritten by later `SetBlendFactor` calls (or simply never set for RT passes) before the single record-time read. Identical shape to the pre-fix Viewport (GFX-062) and Scissor (GFX-013) paths — fix is the same per-draw/per-batch capture.

| Format note | Swapchain prefers `VK_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM` (linear, not sRGB — `1595-1598`), RTs are `VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM` (`3460` etc.). Both linear, so midtone blend-factor values `(64,128,192)` survive the RT-blit→`GetBackBufferData` readback path exactly (no gamma distortion). Vulkan cannot read an RT via `GetData` (no `GetTextureData` impl — `vulkan_orientation_rendertarget_test.cpp:17`), so the test uses the proven GFX-062/013 RT-blit methodology. |

**The fix (`815b33df`, `VulkanGraphicsBackend` only — no shared/interface change).**
1. `Pending3DDraw` + `BatchSnapshot` (hpp): added `blendFactorR/G/B/A` snapshot fields next to the GFX-013/062 scissor/viewport fields (default `1,1,1,1` = XNA `Color::White`, so draws that predate any `SetBlendFactor` use the correct XNA default).
2. `PushPending3DDraw()` (the single 3D enqueue choke point) + `VulkanSpriteBatchBackend::End()`: snapshot the live `blendFactorR_/…` into each draw/batch at enqueue.
3. `RecordCommandBuffer()`: `draw3DFor` (per draw) and `drawSpritesFor` (per batch) replay the captured constant via `vkCmdSetBlendConstants` immediately after the per-draw scissor/viewport, for **both** RT and backbuffer passes. Applied **unconditionally** (Phase 12/15: correctness-first) — the constant is inert for pipelines whose blend factors don't reference `CONSTANT_COLOR`, and issuing it per draw also satisfies `VK_DYNAMIC_STATE_BLEND_CONSTANTS` for every blend-enabled RT draw (fixing the pre-fix VUID below).
4. `SetBlendFactor()` stays store-only; its disclosure comment now describes the per-draw capture. The single backbuffer pass-begin set (6926) is kept (now redundant, overridden per-draw) so a clear-only pass still has a defined constant — mirrors the pass-begin viewport/scissor defaults GFX-062/013 left in place.

**Channel / alpha mapping (Phases 3/5/17).** `float bc[4] = { blendFactorR, G, B, A }` → `vkCmdSetBlendConstants` — direct R→[0], G→[1], B→[2], A→[3]. No BGRA swap, no premultiply, no sRGB (a numeric pipeline factor, not a framebuffer color). The alpha channel feeds the alpha blend-factor slot: for a `VK_BLEND_FACTOR_CONSTANT_COLOR` alpha factor Vulkan uses the constant's `.a`, so the single RGBA set services both color and alpha factors (proven by Frame 3: `AlphaSrc=BlendFactor` exposed `.a`=153 as gray `(153,153,153)` via a two-pass DestinationAlpha readout, since Vulkan can't read RT alpha through the blit).

**Pipeline-cache interaction (Phase 14).** The blend-factor **value** is NOT in the pipeline cache key — only the blend-factor **enums** are hashed (`PackBlendBits`, 3087-3096: `colorSrc/colorDst/alphaSrc/alphaDst/colorFunc/alphaFunc`). The constant lives in `Pending3DDraw`/`BatchSnapshot`, not the pipeline key, so it never fragments the cache. Proven at runtime by Frame 4: three different constants (RED/GREEN/BLUE) through **one** `BlendState` instance → one pipeline → three correct results. Every relevant pipeline already declares `VK_DYNAMIC_STATE_BLEND_CONSTANTS` (2438/2625/2958/3323/4900/5035) — no pipeline change needed.

Vulkan's remaining gap is SpriteBatch-only (GFX-071). |
| Generated shaders | None — zero `.glsl/.vert/.frag/.spv/.hlsl/.wgsl/bytecode/_shaders.hpp` diff (pure command/state handling; blend constant is dynamic pipeline state). |

No bounds arithmetic, no negative/oversized values reach Vulkan (normalization is upstream in `GraphicsDevice`). No dedicated UBSan build warranted (same reasoning as GFX-062/013/069). |
| Deferred-state sweep (Phase 23) | Enumerated every `vkCmdSet*` dynamic pass-state call replayed for queued draws: `vkCmdSetViewport` (per-draw, GFX-062), `vkCmdSetScissor` (per-draw, GFX-013), `vkCmdSetBlendConstants` (per-draw/batch, this task). **Stencil** (`vkCmdSetStencilReference`/`CompareMask`/`WriteMask`) is already captured per draw at enqueue via `draw.dsParams` (`RenderCommandBuffer` reads the snapshot, not a live member) — immune to deferred-replay staleness, no defect. `vkCmdSetDepthBias` is likewise per-draw from `draw.depthBias`. **No remaining Vulkan frame-global stale-state defect** among per-draw dynamic states. |

Broader than a blend-constant bug (the whole BlendState is dropped for sprites); the 3D path already honors it (Task 868). Recorded, NOT fixed (out of GFX-070 scope). ### REMED-GFX-019 — WebGPU: SpriteBatch clip-space mapping is always backbuffer-relative (DONE and VERIFIED, 2026-07-22)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Sev / Pri / Owner / Status | HIGH / P1 / GRAPHICS / **DONE and VERIFIED (WebGPU runtime, wgpu-native v29.0.1.1, Xvfb :99; EasyGL parity, Xvfb :99)** |
| Commits | test `3a0e510d`, fix `be51ec4f`, docs (this entry) |
| Root cause | `WebGPUGraphicsBackend::QueueSprite()` (`src/CNA/Internal/Backends/WebGPU/WebGPUGraphicsBackend.cpp`) baked each sprite's clip-space position CPU-side, at enqueue, from `ComputeLogicalViewport()` (backbuffer virtual-resolution/presentation-mode viewport) and `physicalWidth_/physicalHeight_` (the backbuffer's physical size), with **no** branch on `currentRenderTarget_`/`currentRenderTargetCubeFace_`. WebGPU was the only one of the six SpriteBatch-capable backends hard-coding the backbuffer here (Vulkan/EasyGL/Bgfx/D3D11/SdlGpu all already derive the sprite ortho/NDC from the bound render target's own size — independently source-surveyed for this task). |

**Phase 1 — source reconciliation (CONFIRMED at HEAD).** `ComputeLogicalViewport()` (lines ~4739-4774) is computed exclusively from `physicalWidth_/physicalHeight_/virtualWidth_/virtualHeight_/presentationMode_` — all backbuffer-scoped, no render-target parameter. `QueueSprite()` called it unconditionally and, in the vertex loop, divided the mapped pixel by `physicalWidth_/physicalHeight_` to reach NDC (`2*px/physicalWidth_ - 1`, `1 - 2*py/physicalHeight_`). Neither `currentRenderTarget_` (a `WebGPURenderTargetBackend*`, maintained at bind) nor `currentRenderTargetCubeFace_` was consulted. The self-disclosure in the frozen `examples/webgpu_rendertargetcube_test.cpp` Check-C comment (which deliberately paints the cube faces with a 3D quad instead of SpriteBatch precisely because of this) was re-verified against production source.

**Phase 2 — XNA/FNA semantics.** FNA's `SpriteBatch` maps destination rectangles in the bound target surface's own pixel space, regardless of whether that surface is the backbuffer or a render target; there is no backbuffer-tied "logical viewport" indirection when a render target is bound. Presentation-mode letterbox/stretch/overscan is a backbuffer-only concept (it exists to fit a virtual resolution into a physical window). So a `RenderTarget2D`/`RenderTargetCube` face of size WxH must place `Rectangle(x,y,w,h)` at exactly those target pixels.

**Phase 3 — coordinate pipeline (pre-fix, measured).** Backbuffer 96×72, RT 48×32, `Rectangle(7,5,17,11)`, identity transform: dest corners → pixel points (7,5)..(24,16); backbuffer `ComputeLogicalViewport()` is identity here (`FixedHeightDynamicWidth`, virtual=physical=96×72, matched aspect → logicalWidth=physicalWidth=96) so `px=points.X`, `py=points.Y`; NDC `x=2·px/96-1`, `y=1-2·py/72`; the RT render pass rasterizes into the **full 48×32** target (`viewportSet_` reset to the RT bounds on bind, or clamped to it). Net: the sprite lands at RT ≈x[3.5,12) y[2.2,7.1) — width halved (96/48), height ~0.44 (32/72), shifted to the origin. The correct target is x[7,24) y[5,16). This exactly matches the audit's empirical "only covered one quadrant" note.

**State-lifetime model.** NDC is baked at enqueue into `SpriteCommand.vertices`, accumulated in `spriteCommands_`, and flushed by `RenderSprites(pass)` into whichever pass `FlushCurrentRenderTarget()`/`EnsureFrameRendered()` opens. Crucially, `SetRenderTarget2D()`/`BindAsRenderTargetFace()` call `FlushCurrentRenderTarget()` **before** reassigning the current target, so every sprite in `spriteCommands_` at flush time was enqueued against the currently-bound target — enqueue-time target == render-time target. Therefore the fix belongs in `QueueSprite()` using the *currently-bound* target's size; a per-draw snapshot (Vulkan GFX-062/013 / SdlGpu GFX-064 style) is **not** needed for WebGPU, whose deferred model is target-flushed rather than fully replayed.

**Phase 14 — the fix.** In `QueueSprite()`, before the vertex loop, select the target dimensions and viewport:
- `currentRenderTarget_ != nullptr` → `targetWidth/Height = currentRenderTarget_->GetWidth()/GetHeight()`, identity viewport (x=y=0, width=height=logicalWidth=logicalHeight=target size).
- else `currentRenderTargetCubeFace_ != nullptr` → same, from `GetSize()` (square).
- else → `ComputeLogicalViewport()`, `targetWidth/Height = physicalWidth_/physicalHeight_` (backbuffer path, unchanged).

Then the NDC divide uses `targetWidth/targetHeight` instead of `physicalWidth_/physicalHeight_`. Mirrors `SdlGpuGraphicsBackend::QueueSprite()`'s `currentRenderTarget_` branch, extended to the cube face. The transform matrix (GFX-012 parity) is applied to the pixel-space points **before** this divide, so it is untouched and cannot be double-scaled.

| Test | `examples/webgpu_spritebatch_rendertarget_test.cpp` (`WebGPU_SpriteBatch_RenderTarget`, `cmake/Tests/WebGpuTests.cmake`, TIMEOUT 30). Asymmetric 96×72 backbuffer; solid-white 1×1 texture tinted Red (gamma-invariant); RT pixels read via `RenderTarget2D.GetData` and cube via `RenderTargetCube.GetData`. **23 checks**: A (48×32 RT default Viewport, 6 probes incl. interior=Red-where-pre-fix-is-Black and bug-witness (5,3)=Black-was-Red); B (backbuffer control); C (48×32 vs 64×40 same pixel rect → same RT pixels, catches cached-first-target size); D (RT A→backbuffer→RT B isolation, distinct rects); E (transformMatrix scale 1.5 + translate); F (vertically split texture, PointClamp → no Y-flip); G (RenderTargetCube face 48). |
| Pre-fix vs post-fix (runtime) | **12/23 → 23/23.** Pre-fix: A1 interior (15,10)=`(0,0,0)`, A6 bug-witness (5,3)=`(255,0,0)`, plus C1/C3/D1/D3/E1/F1/F2 fail (sprite mis-scaled off the probes); backbuffer control B passes pre- and post-fix. Post-fix: A1=`(255,0,0)`, A6=`(0,0,0)`, all 23 pass; F top=Red / bottom=Blue (orientation preserved); G face interior=Red. |
| transformMatrix (Phase 10) | Check E: `M11=M22=1.5, M41=2, M42=3` on `Rectangle(4,2,8,6)` → transformed RT rect x[8,20] y[6,15]; interior (14,10)=Red, right-outside (25,10)=Black. Confirms the transform is applied in RT pixel space and converted with RT dims (not double-scaled, not backbuffer-normalized). Pre-fix E1 fails (mapped to ≈x[4,10]). |
| Custom Viewport (Phase 11) | Determined (not asserted in the regression, to avoid coupling GFX-019 to viewport semantics): after the fix, WebGPU bakes sprite NDC over the **full** RT and the render pass additionally applies the device `Viewport` as the rasterizer viewport — so a custom sub-`Viewport` squishes sprites rather than making them viewport-relative. This matches EasyGL/Vulkan/Bgfx/SdlGpu and the pre-existing backbuffer path; only D3D11 is viewport-relative (XNA-correct). The **default** viewport (auto-reset to the full target on `SetRenderTarget`) is correct everywhere. Spawned as **GFX-072** (cross-backend, pre-existing, NOT this defect). |
| UV / orientation (Phase 12) | Check F: a 1×8 red-top/blue-bottom texture drawn PointClamp into the RT reads Red at the target top and Blue at the bottom — the fix changes only the clip-space dimension source, never UV/Y orientation. |
| Render-target types (Phase 17) | RenderTarget2D — AFFECTED, fixed, runtime-verified (A/C/D/E/F). RenderTargetCube face — AFFECTED, fixed, runtime-verified (G — closes the exact gap the frozen cube audit test routed around). MRT — WebGPU has no distinct SpriteBatch-into-MRT geometry path (sprites bind one color attachment); CORRECT-BY-SHARED-PATH, not separately exercised. |
| Validation (Phase 19) | wgpu-native validation (`RUST_LOG=wgpu_core=warn,wgpu_hal=warn`): **zero** buffer-binding-size / uniform-alignment / render-pass-attachment / viewport / shader / pipeline errors before and after. No uniform/buffer layout change (the fix is CPU-side integer selection; no new binding). |
| Regression (Phase 20) | Full WebGPU shard **26/26** (incl. `WebGPU_RenderTarget2D` 8/8, `WebGPU_RenderTargetCube`, `WebGPU_Msaa`, `WebGPU_SkinnedEffect_WorldNormal`=GFX-006 control, `WebGPU_EnvMapEmissive`=GFX-007 control, `WebGPU_TextureCube_GetData`, `WebGPU_MipGen`). Zero regressions. |
| Cross-backend parity (Phase 21) | Independent source survey confirmed Vulkan/EasyGL/Bgfx/D3D11/SdlGpu already divide sprite NDC by the bound RT's size (each backend's exact expression quoted). Empirically confirmed on **EasyGL** — `examples/easygl_spritebatch_rendertarget_size_test.cpp` (`EasyGL_SpriteBatch_RenderTargetSize`, 6/6): the same 96×72/48×32/64×40 geometry yields a **17×11** RT-relative red footprint at x[7..23] (measured bbox), identical to the fixed WebGPU. The test asserts footprint width/height so it is invariant to EasyGL's GL-bottom-left RT-sampling Y-flip (a separate EasyGL convention; the blit reads the sprite at y[16..26] on a 32-tall target). This is a second, non-WebGPU oracle for the required bounds. |
| Generated shaders | None — zero `.wgsl/.glsl/.vert/.frag/.spv/.hlsl/bytecode/_shaders.hpp` diff. The fix is pure CPU-side integer dimension selection; no WGSL change (WebGPU sprite NDC is baked CPU-side, not in a shader uniform). |
| Sanitizers | Low risk: the new arithmetic is `GetWidth()/GetHeight()/GetSize()` (existing ints) fed to the pre-existing `2·px/W-1` float divide; a zero/negative target size is guarded by the existing `targetWidth <= 0 || targetHeight <= 0` early-return (generalized from the old `physicalWidth_ <= 0` guard). No new allocation, no unbounded index, no lifetime change. No dedicated ASan/UBSan run warranted. |
| New findings | **GFX-072** — CNA's SpriteBatch does not thread `GraphicsDevice.Viewport` into the sprite clip-space bake; a custom sub-`Viewport` on a bound target mis-scales sprites on 5/6 backends (D3D11 is XNA-correct). Pre-existing, cross-backend, source-identified, NOT fixed (out of GFX-019 scope). See its table row. |
| Affected files | `src/CNA/Internal/Backends/WebGPU/WebGPUGraphicsBackend.cpp` (fix); `examples/webgpu_spritebatch_rendertarget_test.cpp`, `examples/easygl_spritebatch_rendertarget_size_test.cpp`, `cmake/Tests/WebGpuTests.cmake`, `cmake/Tests/EasyGLTests.cmake` (tests) |
| Backends / Platforms | WebGPU (experimental) / ALL |

### REMED-GFX-072 — SpriteBatch clip space ignores a custom GraphicsDevice.Viewport (DONE and VERIFIED, 2026-07-22)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Sev / Pri / Owner / Status | MEDIUM / P3 / GRAPHICS / **DONE and VERIFIED (Vulkan/SdlGpu/EasyGL/Bgfx/WebGPU runtime, Xvfb :99; D3D11 oracle, Wine+DXVK :0; D3D12 build-verified)** |
| Commits | test `76f5e8a0`; fix Vulkan `166a074b`, SdlGpu `b820a9b8`, EasyGL `dc0e6ca6`, Bgfx `75b99860`, WebGPU `814ebb38`, D3D12 `3fd18152`; D3D11 oracle `e6da0ed5`; docs (this entry) |

**Phase 1 — XNA/FNA contract (PROVEN).** FNA `SpriteBatch.cs` `PrepRenderState()` (lines ~1433-1457) builds the sprite projection as `CreateOrthographicOffCenter(0, Viewport.Width, Viewport.Height, 0, 0, 1) * transformMatrix` from `GraphicsDevice.Viewport` (read live at flush). Therefore sprite destination coordinates are **VIEWPORT-LOCAL**: sprite `(0,0)` is the viewport's top-left corner and `Viewport.Width/Height` define the projection extent. The rasterizer viewport (set separately to `Viewport.X/Y/Width/Height`) maps the `[-1,1]` clip result onto the viewport's screen rectangle. **`Viewport.X/Y` are never subtracted from sprite coordinates** — placement is done entirely by the rasterizer viewport; sprites are 1:1 pixel scale. Confirmed against the D3D11 CNA path (`sprite2d.vert.hlsl`: `ndc = input.Position / ViewportSize * 2 - 1`, with `ViewportSize` = live `RSGetViewports()` width/height) and RUNTIME-PROVEN by the D3D11 oracle test (below), which passes 10/10 unmodified.

**Phase 2 — affected-backend matrix.** Seven SpriteBatch-capable backends bake pixel→NDC themselves; two more delegate; the rest are N/A.

| Backend | Sprite NDC/ortho basis (pre-fix) | Rasterizer viewport | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| D3D11 | live viewport (`RSGetViewports`) | live (`RSSetViewports`) | **ALREADY_CORRECT (oracle)** |
| D3D9 | live viewport (`GetViewport`) ortho | live (`SetViewport`) | ALREADY_CORRECT |
| Vulkan | full target/virtual (push-const `viewportSize`) | per-batch (GFX-062) | **AFFECTED — squish** |
| SdlGpu | full target (shader `viewportSize` uniform) | per-draw (GFX-064) | **AFFECTED — squish** |
| WebGPU | full target (CPU NDC bake) | live at pass (GFX-019) | **AFFECTED — squish** |
| D3D12 | full target (`GetBoundColorWidth/HeightEXT`) | effective (GFX-064) | **AFFECTED — squish** |
| EasyGL | full target/logical ortho | **reset to full target** | **AFFECTED — ignored** |
| Bgfx | full target ortho | **reset to full target** | **AFFECTED — ignored** |
| SDL Renderer | delegates (`SDL_RenderTexture`, logical presentation) | n/a | NOT_APPLICABLE |
| Canvas | delegates (HTML `drawImage`) | n/a | NOT_APPLICABLE |
| Software | CPU raster at raw framebuffer pixels; `SetViewport` no-op | ignored | **SEPARATE_FINDING (GFX-073 — now DONE; spawned GFX-079 3D-path DONE, GFX-080 scissor DONE, GFX-081 SpriteBatch rasterizerState-drop DONE, GFX-082 FillMode-ignored DONE; spawned GFX-083 DepthBias/SlopeScaleDepthBias-ignored NEW)** |
| Dx3 | CPU DirectDraw blt, raw pixels | none | NOT_APPLICABLE |
| Ascii | decorator → inner backend | — | DELEGATES_TO_INNER |
| Headless | records only | records | HEADLESS_NOOP |

Two pre-fix failure modes, both fail the conformance test: **squish** (rasterizer viewport already the sub-region, NDC baked full-target → sprite compressed into the viewport top-left, e.g. 17px → ~7px) and **ignored** (the sprite path also reset the rasterizer viewport to the full target → sprite lands at its raw full-target absolute rect).

**Phases 4-6 — canonical test + D3D11 oracle.** `examples/spritebatch_custom_viewport_test.cpp` (backbuffer `GetBackBufferData` readback — top-left consistent, robust across backends/headless): 96×72 backbuffer, `Viewport(19,11,41,29)`, red sprite viewport-local `Rectangle(5,4,17,11)`. Correct viewport-relative footprint = `x[24,41) y[15,26)` (17×11 at minX 24, minY 15), fully clipped to the viewport rect. Checks: A (custom-viewport footprint width/height/minX/minY + no-red-outside-viewport), B (default full-viewport control — the fix must be a no-op), C (transformMatrix scale 1.5 + translate composed with the custom viewport → 12×9 at (27,17)). `spritebatch_viewport_switch_test.cpp` (Phase 9): two Begin/End batches with different viewports in one frame → each placed by its own batch's viewport (Vulkan per-batch snapshot / SdlGpu per-draw ref / EasyGL immediate-flush). SdlGpu lacks `GetBackBufferData`, so it uses `spritebatch_custom_viewport_rt_test.cpp` (RenderTarget2D `GetData` readback, which flushes the deferred batch; bbox-based, Y-orientation-invariant) covering all four scenes. **D3D11 oracle** (`D3D11_SpriteBatch_CustomViewport`, Wine+DXVK :0): the SAME test, **10/10 with NO D3D11 code change** → footprint `x[24,40] y[15,25] n=187` — runtime proof of the viewport-relative contract.

**Phases 11-15,20 — per-backend fixes** (each gated on a genuine custom sub-region so the default full-target path is byte-identical; virtual-resolution/letterbox preserved).
- **Vulkan** (`fix 166a074b`): `drawSpritesFor` now feeds the sprite2d push-constant `viewportSize` from the batch's captured `Viewport.W/H` (GFX-062 snapshot) instead of `virtualWidth_/swapchainExtent`/`rt->GetWidth`. Vertices already raw viewport-local. GFX-011 Y-flip / GFX-012 transform / GFX-013 scissor / GFX-070 blend untouched. `4/12 → 10/10`; switch `3/6 → 6/6`.
- **SdlGpu** (`fix b820a9b8`): `QueueSprite()` bakes raw viewport-local pixels (no letterbox) when custom; `RenderQueuedDraws` feeds `IssueSpriteDraw` the per-`QueuedDrawRef` `Viewport.W/H` (GFX-064) as the shader divisor. `3/8 → 8/8` (RT test, incl. switch + transform).
- **EasyGL** (`fix dc0e6ca6`): `FlushBatch()` reads the live GL viewport (which survives `Clear` — Task 880) and, when a custom sub-region, sizes the ortho to `Viewport.W/H` and LEAVES the custom GL viewport in place (previously reset to full + full-target ortho). `6/10 → 10/10`; switch `6/6`.
- **Bgfx** (`fix 75b99860`): captures the `Viewport` at sprite submit (`spriteVp*`, survives a restore before Present; reset per frame); when custom, an **OFFSET ortho** (`screen = Viewport.XY + local`, 1:1 scale) over a still-**FULL** sprite view rect. Full rect is mandatory because in bgfx the view rect is ALSO the `setViewClear` region — a sub-region rect would scope `Clear()` to it (violating XNA clear-the-whole-target; this was caught by a 3-scene multi-readback sequence leaving stale content). `6/10 → 10/10`. Deviation: sprites exceeding the viewport are not hard-clipped at the viewport edge; multiple viewports/view/frame remain last-wins (**GFX-065, NOT resolved**).
- **WebGPU** (`fix 814ebb38`): `QueueSprite()` bakes viewport-relative NDC (divide by `viewportW_/H_`) and captures the `Viewport` into each `SpriteCommand`; `RenderSprites()` drives the rasterizer viewport **per draw** from the capture (necessary because WebGPU records the pass viewport live at flush — after a restore; `RenderSprites` runs last so it can't disturb the 3D draws). Preserves GFX-019 RT-size selection. `5/10 → 10/10`. No WGSL diff.
- **D3D12** (`fix 3fd18152`, build-verified): `FlushBatch()` uses `GetEffectiveViewportEXT().Width/Height` for the sprite2d `ViewportSize` projection basis (was `GetBoundColorWidth/HeightEXT`) — a line-for-line analog of the D3D11 oracle. Scissor stays full target. Runtime pixel readback deferred (off-screen `BindOffscreenColorTargetEXT` + READBACK-heap EXT scaffolding under Wine+vkd3d, not the standard XNA readback the shared test uses).

**Phase 23 — cross-backend numerical parity.** The canonical scene renders to the **byte-identical** footprint `x[24,40] y[15,25] n=187` on **D3D11 (unmodified oracle), Vulkan, SdlGpu, EasyGL, Bgfx, and WebGPU**. Transform check `x[27,38] y[17,25] n=108` identical on all backbuffer backends.

**Phase 22 — regressions.** Full backend shards, all graphics/sprite/RT/viewport/scissor/blend tests green: Vulkan 5770/5774, SdlGpu, EasyGL, Bgfx, WebGPU (incl. GFX-012/013/019/062/063/064/068/070 controls and both new GFX-072 tests). Every shard's remaining failures (`Cnj*` content fixtures, `GraphicsDeviceCapabilityTest.DoesNotSupportWireFrame` on llvmpipe, ENet/sound/ContentManager, `WebGPU_Clear_Readback`, `Bgfx_*Msaa*`/`*DepthFormat`) were confirmed to fail **identically with each fix stashed** — pre-existing/environmental, none touch the 2D sprite path.

**Generated artifacts / sanitizers.** No generated-shader diff (WGSL/GLSL/HLSL/SPIR-V/`_shaders.hpp` all unchanged — the fixes are CPU-side dimension/divisor selection and one added CPU ortho; the D3D/Vulkan/SdlGpu sprite shaders were untouched). Sanitizers: the new arithmetic is `GetWidth()/viewportW_` integer selection feeding pre-existing float divides, all guarded against zero/degenerate viewports; no new allocation, index, or lifetime — no dedicated ASan/UBSan run warranted.

| New findings | **GFX-073** — Software backend `SpriteBatchBackend` rasterizes sprites at raw framebuffer pixel coordinates and its `SetViewport` is a no-op, so a custom `Viewport` neither positions nor clips sprites. Not the mis-scale defect; a broader Software-2D viewport gap — its own task. **NOW DONE** (see the GFX-073 row above); the original parenthetical "the 3D path does use the viewport" proved INACCURATE on source inspection (the 3D path maps NDC over the full framebuffer via `GetViewportSize`, no viewport X/Y/W/H/depth-range) → spawned **GFX-079** (3D-path viewport gap) and **GFX-080** (`SetScissorRect` no-op). **GFX-074** — Vulkan defers SpriteBatch-into-`RenderTarget2D` to Present: reading the RT via `GetData` before Present returns cleared content (sprites not flushed), and destroying the `RenderTarget2D` before Present leaves a dangling `batchRT` pointer in `activeBatches_` → use-after-free at the next Present. Surfaced while building the GFX-072 harness (worked around by using the backbuffer path for Vulkan). |

## REMED-GFX-074 — Vulkan deferred RenderTarget2D GetData synchronization + target lifetime

**Status:** DONE and VERIFIED (feature/audit). Test `b129825c`, fix `202211b6`.
**Scope:** Vulkan backend only (`VulkanGraphicsBackend.{cpp,hpp}`). Memory-safety + correctness.

### Root cause (generic to the target identity, not SpriteBatch-specific)

The Vulkan backend records the *entire* frame lazily in `RecordCommandBuffer` at Present. Draws
and clears issued while a `RenderTarget2D` is bound are appended to three deferred queues, each
tagging the work with a **raw `VulkanRTSource*`** (the target's identity):

- `activeBatches_` — `std::pair<unique_ptr<BatchSnapshot>, VulkanRTSource*>` (SpriteBatch)
- `pending3D_` — `Pending3DDraw{ …, VulkanRTSource* rt; }` (3D draws)
- `clearedRTs_` — `std::vector<VulkanRTSource*>` (bare `Clear()` with no draw)

`RecordCommandBuffer` builds `usedRTs` from all three, then (Phase 1) opens each target's render
pass and replays its sprites + 3D draws; only then (Phase 2) does the backbuffer pass run.

Two independent defects fell out of this:

1. **Lifetime / UAF.** `~VulkanRenderTargetBackend` removed itself from `liveRenderTargets_` and
   cleared `currentRT_`, but **left its `VulkanRTSource*` in the deferred queues**. Destroying a
   `RenderTarget2D` after queuing work into it but before Present left a dangling pointer that the
   next Present's `usedRTs` loop dereferenced (`rt->GetColorAttachmentCount()`,
   `rt->GetRenderPass()`, `rt->GetFramebuffer()`) → **heap-use-after-free / SIGSEGV**. The bug is
   about the *target identity*, so 3D draws (`pending3D_`) and bare clears (`clearedRTs_`) dangle
   exactly like sprites — not a SpriteBatch-only defect.

2. **GetData visibility.** `VulkanRenderTargetBackend` never overrode
   `ITextureBackend::GetData(level,x,y,w,h,data,len)`. `Texture2D::GetData` zero-fills its buffer
   then calls the backend for a GPU-only render target, hitting the **base no-op** → all-zeros.
   Even conceptually, the target's deferred work is not recorded until Present, so nothing existed
   to read back. (Existing Vulkan RT tests dodged this by sampling the RT onto the backbuffer and
   using `GetBackBufferData`, which *does* force a submit.)

### Ownership graph (before → after)

```
RenderTarget2D (XNA, shared_ptr<ITextureBackend>)
        │ owns
        ▼
VulkanRenderTargetBackend  ── is-a ──▶ VulkanRTSource  (raw* captured into queues)
        │ owns
        ▼
colorImage_ / framebuffer_ / renderPass  (freed in ReleaseVulkanResources)

BEFORE:  ~VulkanRenderTargetBackend frees GPU resources, leaves raw VulkanRTSource*
         in activeBatches_/pending3D_/clearedRTs_  →  Present derefs freed memory (UAF)
AFTER:   ~VulkanRenderTargetBackend calls PurgeDeferredWorkForTarget(this) first, so no
         deferred entry outlives the target it references. RenderTargetCube destructor does
         the same for its 6 face proxies.
```

Raw references audited in the deferred entries: the target `VulkanRTSource*` (this fix); vertex/
index/instance bytes are **copies** (safe); sampler `VkDescriptorSet`s, custom-effect pointers and
occlusion-query pointers are **borrowed and can dangle** — a *different* reference path, filed as
**GFX-075** (Phase 25 below), not fixed here.

### Chosen architecture — target-scoped flush + purge-on-destroy

- **UAF:** `PurgeDeferredWorkForTarget(VulkanRTSource*)` erases every entry referencing the dying
  target from all three queues; called from `~VulkanRenderTargetBackend` and (per face proxy)
  `~VulkanRenderTargetCubeBackend`, before `ReleaseVulkanResources`. Narrow, no GPU stall.
  **Semantics:** a destroyed target is unobservable — its `GetData` can no longer be called, and
  sampling its freed image is already broken independently — so dropping its unflushed draws is
  observationally identical to XNA's eager model, where those draws had already executed by the
  time the resource was disposed. (Flush-on-destroy was rejected: a device-wide stall on every RT
  disposal, with no observable benefit over the purge.)
- **GetData visibility:** `RecordCommandBuffer` gains a `RecordMode::RenderTargetsOnly` that records
  exactly one target's off-screen pass into a transient command buffer — **skips Phase 2 (no
  backbuffer, no swapchain image, no present, no frame-bookkeeping advance)** and consumes only that
  target's deferred entries so Present never replays them (no double-render). `FlushDeferredRenderTarget(rt)`
  drives it (`vkDeviceWaitIdle` → record → submit → `vkQueueWaitIdle`), a no-op when nothing is
  queued for `rt`. `VulkanRenderTargetBackend::GetData` calls it, then reads `colorImage_` back via
  a host-visible staging buffer (`vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer`, SHADER_READ_ONLY↔TRANSFER_SRC transitions,
  swapchain **BGRA→RGBA** swap since the RT uses `swapchainFormat_`), mirroring
  `VulkanTexture3DBackend::GetData`.

This is **target-scoped** (a `GetData` on RT-A never forces RT-B or the backbuffer through a fake
Present) and reuses the exact per-draw/batch replay path, so GFX-013 scissor / GFX-062 viewport /
GFX-070 blend-constant / GFX-072 viewport-relative sprite projection / GFX-012 transform are all
preserved unchanged.

### CPU/GPU synchronization

`GetData` is a hard sync point (allowed by design). The flush waits the device idle first (so no
in-flight frame is using the shared per-frame sprite/3D ring buffers it reuses), submits the
off-screen pass, and `vkQueueWaitIdle`s before the readback copy — render writes happen-before the
transfer read via the RT render pass's `SHADER_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL` finalLayout plus the
`GetData` layout transition. **The normal Present path is untouched** — no global wait or flush is
added to ordinary SpriteBatch/3D rendering; the cost is paid only inside `GetData` and only when the
target has pending work.

### XNA/FNA + cross-backend semantics (Phase 24)

`RenderTarget2D::GetData`-before-Present is supported by exactly three backends, and **all three
flush inside GetData**: Vulkan (this fix, `FlushDeferredRenderTarget`), WebGPU
(`RenderPendingDrawsToRenderTarget`), SdlGpu (`EnsureFrameRendered`). The other six
(EasyGL/Bgfx/D3D11/D3D12/D3D9/SdlRenderer) never override the 2D-texture/RT `GetData` and return the
frontend's zero-filled buffer — a broader cross-backend gap, out of scope here. So this fix aligns
Vulkan with the established deferred-backend contract rather than inventing one.

  visibility w/ spatial probes (red block on black clear, count ≈ 20×16=320), S2 two batches
  composite, S3 two independent RTs each read their own content, S4 content survives a later Present
  (consumed batch not re-cleared), S5 mixed 3D(left half)+2D(right half) both flushed, S6

- **RT-readback GFX-072 variant** (`spritebatch_custom_viewport_rt_test.cpp`) now runs **directly

- **ASan pre-fix reproduction:** with the destructor purge disabled, `heap-use-after-free` READ at

- **Vulkan validation:** `VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation` confirmed loaded (loader debug) — **zero VUIDs**

- **Generated artifacts:** none — CPU-side backend logic + one new test; no shader/SPIR-V diff.

### Phase 25 — deferred-resource lifetime sweep → new finding GFX-075

Read-only audit of every raw reference a deferred entry retains: the target `VulkanRTSource*` is
fixed here; vertex/index/instance data is copied (safe); but **sampler descriptor sets (the
`VkImageView` they bake), custom-effect pointers/pipelines, and occlusion-query pointers are borrowed
and dangle if their resource is destroyed before Present** — the same UAF class through a different
reference path that `PurgeDeferredWorkForTarget` (destination-keyed) does not cover. Filed as
**GFX-075**; not fixed opportunistically (separable ownership model).

## REMED-GFX-075 — Vulkan deferred SOURCE-resource lifetime (generic retirement ownership)

**Status:** DONE and VERIFIED (feature/audit). Test `ac4abd50`, fix `2416b8de`.
**Scope:** Vulkan backend only (`VulkanGraphicsBackend.{cpp,hpp}`) + one new test. Memory-safety +
API-ordering. Same UAF *class* as GFX-074, different (source-resource) reference paths.

### Generic root cause

Vulkan records the *entire* frame lazily in `RecordCommandBuffer` at Present (or, for a mid-frame
`RenderTarget2D::GetData`, in GFX-074's target-scoped `RenderTargetsOnly` flush). A deferred entry
(`pending3D_` / `activeBatches_` / `clearedRTs_`) therefore **borrows GPU resources owned by the
SOURCE objects a draw samples/uses**, and those objects can be legally destroyed by the application
the moment the public `Draw()` / `SpriteBatch.End()` returns — long before the record runs. GFX-074
fixed only the *destination* target identity (`d.rt`/`batchRT`, via `PurgeDeferredWorkForTarget`).
The source paths were unprotected: destroying the resource immediately freed the `VkImageView` baked
into a captured descriptor set, the custom effect's `VkPipeline`, or the query's `VkQueryPool`, which
`RecordCommandBuffer` then bound/dereferenced → heap-use-after-free + Vulkan lifetime VUID.

### Complete affected-resource inventory (Phase 1 / 10)

| Deferred reference | Held in | Owner | User-destroyable before record? | Pre-fix safety | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Pending3DDraw::descSet` / effect descsets (`dualTex/envMap/skinned/pbr/litTextured/fogTex3D`) → their baked `VkImageView` | `pending3D_` | texture/cube/RT backends | yes | **DANGLE** | retirement of the view |
| sprite `DrawCall::descSet` → baked texture `VkImageView` | `activeBatches_`→`BatchSnapshot` | texture/RT backend | yes | **DANGLE** | retirement of the view + `texSamplerDescSets_` eviction |
| `BatchSnapshot::customEffectBackend` (raw ptr) → `VkPipeline`/`VkPipelineLayout`/`GetPushConst()` | `activeBatches_` | `VulkanEffectBackend` | yes | **DANGLE (ptr+pipeline)** | snapshot pipeline/layout/PC **by value** at End() + retire pipeline/layout/modules |
| `Pending3DDraw::occlusionQuery` (raw ptr) → `->pool_`/`->recordedThisFrame_` | `pending3D_` | `VulkanOcclusionQueryBackend` | yes | **DANGLE (ptr+pool)** | `PurgeDeferredQuery` detach (draw kept) + retire pool |
| MRT proxy pointer (`d.rt`) → `GetFramebuffer()`/`GetRenderPass()` | all queues | `mrtProxy_` | yes (SetRenderTargets replaces it) | **DANGLE (object)** | retire the whole proxy object, don't destroy under queued work |
| target `VulkanRTSource*` (`d.rt`/`batchRT`) | all queues | RT/cube | yes | SAFE | already GFX-074 (`PurgeDeferredWorkForTarget`) |
| vertex/index/instance bytes | `vbData`/`ibData`/`instVbData`, `BatchSnapshot::vertices/indices` | the entry | n/a | SAFE (copied at enqueue) | unchanged |

### API semantic contract (Phase 3, confirmed vs D3D11/EasyGL/FNA)

A deferred backend must be **observationally immediate**: once `Draw()`/`SpriteBatch.End()` returns,
the resource is *logically consumed*. Disposing it afterwards must not retroactively cancel the draw,
change the sampled texture, invalidate the pipeline, or crash. (Immediate backends already behave
this way: the GPU command referencing the resource was issued at the call, so a later dispose cannot
un-issue it.) Therefore the fix **retains** source resources until the deferred draw is consumed — it
never purges/drops them the way GFX-074 legitimately drops *destination* work (a destroyed
destination is unobservable; a destroyed source of an already-issued draw is not).

### Architecture selected — frame-fence-tagged retirement queue (Phase 11)

Chose **option B (backend deferred-destruction / retirement queue)** over per-entry `shared_ptr`
ownership (A/C: invasive, per-draw refcount churn, would still not stop a wrapper-pointer deref) —
plus two targeted source-side fixes for the two cases that dereference a C++ *wrapper* (effect
push-constants, query bookkeeping) rather than a pure handle. This is the single generic mechanism
the task asked for, and it covers **both** lifetime windows (Phase 13): the CPU record window (a
deferred entry still holds the handle) *and* the GPU execution window (submitted work still reads it).

- **`RetiredResources`** bag (views/images/memory/framebuffers/pipelines/layouts/modules/query
  pools/descriptor sets) + `retiredResources_`, `retiredMrtProxies_`, and a `frameGeneration_` clock.
- Every user-destroyable resource destructor now calls `RetireResources()` (tagging with
  `frameGeneration_`) **instead of `vkDestroy…` + `vkDeviceWaitIdle`**. The per-destroy device stall
  is *removed*, not added (Phase 14/21): retirement subsumes it with a strictly wider safety window.
- **`ProcessRetiredResources(false)`** runs once per frame at `SubmitFrame`'s
  `vkWaitForFences(inFlightFences_[currentFrame_])` sync point and frees a bucket only when
  `generation + MaxFramesInFlight < frameGeneration_`. `frameGeneration_` is bumped after each Full
  submit. A bucket retired at generation G is (at most) consumed by the Full record at G+1, whose
  fence is guaranteed signalled before generation G+1+MaxFramesInFlight begins (frame-slot reuse
  waits it) — so the condition is strictly conservative. No `vkDeviceWaitIdle` on the ordinary path.
- **Teardown:** `~VulkanGraphicsBackend` force-drains (`ProcessRetiredResources(true)`) after its
  Step-1 device wait and after the live-resource `ReleaseVulkanResources()` calls, before the
  descriptor pool is destroyed (retired sets are freed from it).

### Per-resource implementation

- **Texture2D / RenderTarget2D-as-sampler / TextureCube / RenderTargetCube:** `ReleaseVulkanResources`
  / destructor retire all handles; `EvictSampledViewFromCaches` drops+retires the persistent
  `texSamplerDescSets_` entries keyed on the dying 2D view (closes the handle-reuse stale-cache risk).
  RT/cube keep GFX-074's destination purge for their *own* queued work.
- **Custom Effect:** `BatchSnapshot` now stores `hasCustomEffect`/`customPipeline`/`customLayout`/
  `customPushConst[32]` captured **by value at `End()`** (effect still alive); `RecordCommandBuffer`
  reads those, never the wrapper. `~VulkanEffectBackend` retires the pipeline/layout/modules.
- **OcclusionQuery:** `~VulkanOcclusionQueryBackend` calls `PurgeDeferredQuery(this)` (nulls the
  borrowed pointer in every pending draw — the draw is preserved, only the now-unobservable query
  correlation is dropped) and retires the `VkQueryPool`.
- **MRT (Phase 9):** `SetRenderTargets` moves the outgoing `mrtProxy_` into `retiredMrtProxies_`
  (freed after the same generation gate) rather than destroying it while its already-queued render
  work legitimately awaits Present — the proxy pointer stored as `d.rt` stays valid. This is the
  "stable identity, don't destroy the wrapper under queued work" resolution the phase asked for; the
  underlying `VulkanRenderTargetBackend` attachments are independently retired by their own backends.

### Verification (llvmpipe, Xvfb :99; validation layer loaded — proven by the pre-fix VUIDs)

- **Pre-fix ASan reproduction:** the new test under ASan emits the Vulkan validation lifetime VUID
  *"the combined image sampler descriptor … is using imageView … invalid or has been destroyed"*
  (`VUID-vkCmdDrawIndexed-None-08114`), S1 FAILs (garbage, not red), then **`AddressSanitizer: SEGV`**
  in `libvulkan_lvp` reading the freed image. Post-fix: **8/8 PASS, exit 0, zero `[Vulkan Validation]`
  lines, no SEGV.** Draw-preservation confirmed by content (S1 red, S2 green ×10, S3 blue RT-sample,
  S4/S5 red-tinted, S6 shows the destroyed texture's colour despite an intervening realloc).
- **GFX-074 regression (Phase 22/23):** `Vulkan_RenderTarget_GetDataLifetime` **13/13** under ASan,
  validation-clean — target-scoped GetData flush, consume-once, destroy-destination all preserved.
- **Adjacent regressions:** `Vulkan_OcclusionQuery` 6/6 (live-query path intact after the query-dtor
  change), `vulkan_shader_effect` PASS (effect-by-value snapshot), `vulkan_env_map` PASS (cube).
- **Full Vulkan ctest:** **5772 passed / 5 skipped / 5 failed out of 5777.** All 5 failures are
  pre-existing/environmental and unrelated: `GraphicsDeviceCapabilityTest.DoesNotSupportWireFrame`
  (llvmpipe *does* support wireframe), `CnjEffectTest.LoadsRealCnjFixture`,
  `CnjStockEffectTest.CustomGlslEffectStillWorks` (all three the documented GFX-074 baseline trio),
  `Vulkan_DepthBias` (**verified identical 3/4 on the stashed baseline** with my edits reverted — an
  llvmpipe constant-depth-bias quirk), and `ENetDiscoveryServiceTest.UnregisterHostStopsAnsweringQueries`
  (flaky under `-j2`, **passes in isolation** — network/timing, not graphics).

### Performance / memory (Phase 27)

Retention window is bounded: a resource retired during frame N is freed at frame ~N+`MaxFramesInFlight`+1
(≤3 frames), at the fence-wait sync point already present. No whole-texture payload is copied — only
lightweight Vulkan handles move to `RetiredResources`, and the effect snapshot copies a 128-byte
push-constant block. No per-draw refcount churn. Net: the ordinary destruction path is now **faster**
(the pre-existing per-destroy `vkDeviceWaitIdle` device stall is gone), at the cost of a bounded,
small deferred-free walk once per frame.

### Final deferred-reference inventory (Phase 29) — no unexplained dangling-risk references remain

Every pointer/handle held across API-return → record is now: **copied by value** (vertex/index/instance
bytes, effect push-constants), **retained until consumed** (all sampled `VkImageView`s, effect
`VkPipeline`/layout, query `VkQueryPool`, MRT proxy object), **protected by target-specific purge**
(destination `VulkanRTSource*`, GFX-074), or **backend-global lifetime** (default white/flat/cube
fallbacks, samplers, per-frame ring buffers — not user-destroyable).

### Generated artifacts

**None.** CPU-side backend logic + one new test only; `git status` shows no `.glsl`/`.spv`/shader
changes (`spirv_shaders.hpp` untouched).

### New finding spawned → GFX-076 (narrow residual)

The **per-frame effect descriptor-set caches** (`dualTexDescSets_`/`envMapDescSets_`/
`litTexturedDescSets_`/`fogTex3DDescSets_`/`skinnedDescSets_`/`pbrDescSets_`/`pbrSkinnedDescSets_`)
key on a hash of raw view pointers and persist across frames with no free path until teardown.
Retirement keeps a dying view alive through the consume window (so the **UAF is fixed** — the GPU
never reads freed memory), but *after* the view is finally freed its `VkImageView` handle value could
be reused by a new texture whose hash collides, returning a stale cached set that samples the wrong
(destroyed) image. Unlike `texSamplerDescSets_` (now evicted per-view), these caches cannot be
cheaply evicted by view (hash-keyed) and clearing them mid-run would leak their pool-allocated sets.
**GFX-076:** rekey or generation-stamp the per-frame effect descriptor caches so a reused view handle
cannot alias a stale entry (or give them a proper per-view eviction/free path).
